hero.subheadline: Poster designers explore what remains human in the age of AI
hero.valueProposition: Free-entry social design contest with a €2,500 Favini Mention and €1,500 Fondazione Time2 Mention, judged by graphic design experts.

content.whyJoin:
Posterheroes is an established international contest about social communication that calls for posters on social and environmental issues. The 15th edition, themed Still Human, invites designers and creatives to explore the jagged boundary between delegation and responsibility, automation and choice, efficiency and creativity in the age of artificial intelligence.

The competition is free to enter and open to students, professional designers, and anyone interested in graphic design. Each participant may submit up to three unpublished posters of 70x100cm, with all text in English. The jury is composed of relevant graphic design and visual communication experts who select 40 winning posters from a pool of 150 finalists.

Posterheroes is organized by the non-profit Cultural Association Plug with the support of Favini, ITC-ILO, Fondazione Time2, Print Club Torino, and Graphic Days. Winners receive the Favini Mention of €2,500 and the Fondazione Time2 Mention of €1,500, and authors of winning works receive a copy of the 2027 Calendar produced by Favini.
content.whoShouldApply:
This contest is for designers and creatives of any age or nationality who want to use poster design for social communication. It welcomes students, professional designers, and anyone interested in graphic design, whether participating as individuals or as groups.

The Still Human theme speaks to designers thinking about technology, artificial intelligence, human agency, and authorship. Participants create unpublished posters on social themes, with all text in English.

This call suits graphic designers who want their work judged by leading visual communication experts and who are comfortable creating impactful 70x100cm posters on contemporary social issues.

faq.question: What is the theme for the 15th edition?
faq.answer: The theme is Still Human, exploring the boundary between delegation and responsibility, automation and choice, efficiency and creativity in the age of artificial intelligence. The goal is to make the effects and imaginaries of technology visible.

faq.question: Who can participate and how many posters can be submitted?
faq.answer: The competition is open to creatives of any age or nationality, including students, professional designers, and individuals or groups. Each participant may submit up to three posters.

faq.question: What are the poster requirements?
faq.answer: Posters must be unpublished, sized 70x100cm, with all text in English. Posters are submitted digitally through the upload section on the Posterheroes website.

faq.question: What are the prizes?
faq.answer: The Favini Mention awards €2,500 and the Fondazione Time2 Mention awards €1,500, with more mentions announced later. Authors of the 40 winning posters receive a copy of the 2027 Calendar produced by Favini.

faq.question: When is the submission deadline?
faq.answer: The submission deadline is August 16, 2026 at 11:59 CEST. The original deadline was July 31, 2026, and it was extended.

faq.question: Who organizes Posterheroes?
faq.answer: Posterheroes is a project by the non-profit Cultural Association Plug, in collaboration with Favini, ITC-ILO, Fondazione Time2, Print Club Torino, and Graphic Days.

submissionGuide.detail: Download the official brief and regulation for the 15th edition from the Posterheroes website to understand the theme, rules, and submission requirements.
Design up to three unpublished posters of 70x100cm on the Still Human theme, ensuring all text is in English and your work is original.
Register on the upload section of the Posterheroes website to create your participant account.
Upload up to 3 posters before the deadline of August 16, 2026 at 11:59 CEST. Keep your open file ready to authenticate your creation if selected.
The jury selects 40 winning posters from the finalists. Winning authors receive the prizes and a copy of the 2027 Calendar.
